articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5 in mid-April 2026, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning across text, image, audio, and video inputs with a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates significant improvements in long-horizon planning tasks and scientific reasoning benchmarks, narrowing the gap on several domain-expert evaluations. Enterprise API access is rolling out with new structured-output guarantees and a refined function-calling protocol.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2 solved 88% of International Mathematical Olympiad-level problems in a controlled evaluation, a jump from approximately 72% achieved by its predecessor. The system uses a novel verify-and-refine chain-of-thought architecture that iteratively checks its own proof steps. The result reignites debate about whether LLMs are developing genuine mathematical reasoning or sophisticated pattern matching at scale.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Demonstrates Fully Autonomous Warehouse Shift with Figure 03 Humanoids
articles.summary: Figure completed a 10-hour autonomous warehouse operations demo in Houston where a fleet of eight Figure 03 humanoid robots handled picking, packing, and palletizing without human intervention. The robots used on-device vision-language models for real-time object identification and grasp planning, achieving a 97.3% successful pick rate across irregular item geometries. BMW and Amazon are reportedly in advanced procurement talks for pilot deployments.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Gains Fine Manipulation Skills with New Dexterous End Effectors
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics unveiled an upgraded electric Atlas platform equipped with 16-degree-of-freedom hands capable of tool use, cable routing, and delicate assembly tasks. Internal benchmarks show the robot threading bolts, operating power tools, and handling flexible materials with sub-millimeter precision. The company positions the update as critical for its Hyundai manufacturing integration slated for Q3 2026.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Constitutional Classifiers' Framework for Real-Time AI Safety Monitoring
articles.summary: Anthropic published a new open-source framework called Constitutional Classifiers that allows organizations to attach lightweight, interpretable safety monitors to any LLM deployment in production. The classifiers run as sidecar processes evaluating model outputs against customizable policy constitutions with less than 15ms added latency. Early adopters report a 60% reduction in policy-violating outputs compared to prompt-based guardrails alone.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm A14 Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that its Fab 21 in Arizona has commenced volume production on the A14 (1.4nm-class) process node, approximately two months ahead of the original timeline. The node uses gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and backside power delivery, yielding an estimated 20% performance gain and 30% power reduction over N2. Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD are all confirmed first customers, with AI accelerator dies expected to ship in Q3 2026.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Approval for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Trial
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to begin human trials of its N2 implant, which doubles electrode count to 2,048 channels and adds bidirectional stimulation capabilities. The second-generation device targets both motor restoration for paralysis patients and a new exploratory indication for treatment-resistant depression. The approval follows 18 months of data from the first-generation PRIME study, where participants demonstrated sustained cursor and robotic arm control.

articles.title: Toyota Research Institute Unveils Diffusion-Policy Framework for Generalizable Robot Learning
articles.summary: TRI published a landmark paper and open-source release of a diffusion-policy-based robot learning framework that enables household manipulation robots to generalize across hundreds of unseen objects and tasks after training on only 50 demonstration episodes per skill. The approach combines 3D diffusion policies with a foundation world model pre-trained on internet-scale video. In standardized benchmarks the system outperformed prior sim-to-real methods by 40% on novel task success rate.
